The story, tap by tap

The 14-step pitch journey

Thandi, a final-year student, from signing in to giving back as an alumna. These are real screenshots, taken by the automated test that runs the journey on every change. Swipe sideways; tap a screen to enlarge it.

For the teams who run it

The operator console

Communications, faculties, approvers and commerce staff publish into their own areas, and nobody approves their own notice. Every action is permission-checked and written to an audit log.

Evidence

What’s built

51app screens
15console pages
4roles
14system adapters
~29klines of code
126unit tests
184screens checked per run
0NMU endpoints invented
  • Product discovery & UX/UI design. Design system on the C.I. palette and Nunito Sans; every flow for four roles, with loading, empty, error, offline and denied states.
  • Mobile app (iOS, Android, web). 51 screens, four roles, the 14-step pitch journey, offline rules, accessibility patterns, assistant, payments and tickets on demo data.
  • Operator console. 15 pages: notifications workflow, approvals, audiences, events, commerce, content, moderation, roles, analytics, audit log.
  • Backend (BFF) & system integrations. The contract: 14 typed adapters and 65 routes, an error model and mock implementations of every system.
  • Security, privacy & compliance. Role-based access in one policy, student-controlled parent consent, tokens in the device keychain, no caching of money, results or wellbeing.
  • Testing & accessibility. 126 unit tests, the pitch journey end to end, a 184-screen sweep, automated WCAG 2.2 AA checks on the console, CI.
  • Hosting, DevOps & release. Continuous integration for the app and the console.
  • Project management, content & launch. Brief analysis, documentation, integration contract and handover.

Checks passing: typecheck, lint and 126 unit tests; the 14-step journey in a browser; every screen for four roles at two phone widths; WCAG 2.2 AA automated checks on all 15 console pages; both GitHub workflows green.

Audit

How much is left

“Complete” means two different things, so there are two answers.

The prototype: 90% complete

Measured against the brief’s definition of done (§30). What’s left is mostly inputs from NMU, plus device testing:

  • Run the native iOS and Android builds on real phones and fix what turns up. Everything so far has been tested in the web build.
  • NMU confirms the university’s name in the app and supplies the approved logo.
  • The Alumni Mentorship photograph (a stand-in is used today).
  • Protection Services confirms the Campus Protection numbers.
  • Each owner approves or rewrites their help article for the assistant.
  • A manual VoiceOver and TalkBack pass.

A production launch: 32% complete

Real students on real data, in the app stores. About 146 of 214 person-weeks remain. Most of it is the backend that connects NMU’s systems, which hasn’t been started: the prototype runs on demo data by design.

Estimate

What it costs

Priced at South African agency rates for a team covering product, design, mobile, web, backend, QA, security and delivery. A budget estimate for planning, not a quote.

To finish from todayR5.0mRange R3.5m – R7.7m · ≈ US$300kWith 15% contingency: R5.7m
Full build from scratchR7.3mRange R5.1m – R11.3m · ≈ US$441kWith 15% contingency: R8.4m
Work already in placeR2.3m≈ 68 person-weeks at the likely rateWhat the prototype would cost to commission

Timeline and team

  • To launch from today: about 21 weeks of work for a team of 7; plan for 6–8 months, because access to NMU’s systems and approvals set the pace.
  • From scratch: about 31 weeks of work; plan for 9–12 months.
  • Team: a delivery lead or business analyst, a product designer, two app and web developers, two backend and integration developers and a QA and accessibility tester. Part-time: security and DevOps.

Assumptions

  • Blended agency rate R850/hour (range R700–R1,100), 40-hour weeks. Senior developers earn roughly R420–R630/hour employed and bill about US$40–55/hour through outsourcing firms.
  • Effort could run 15% under or 20% over the model, mostly depending on how easily NMU’s systems can be reached.
  • US$1 ≈ R16.50. Excludes VAT, third-party licences and NMU’s own staff time.
  • Scope: everything in the brief, built as one phase. Launching the pitch-journey services first and adding the rest later spreads the cost.

Next steps

What NMU needs to provide

  • Access to systems. API or data access to SSO, the student system, finance, LMS, library, transport, residence and the alumni CRM. The biggest single unknown in the estimate.
  • Identity. An OIDC client registered for NMU ONE with NMU SSO.
  • Providers. Payment, donations, push notifications and campus mapping.
  • Policy. Parent access rules, POPIA advice, digital ID approval.
  • Content owners. Named owners for help articles, safety information and notices.

Biggest risk: how NMU’s systems can be reached. Systems with modern APIs keep the integration estimate; systems that need exports, middleware or vendor work push it towards the high end.
